answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every identity to lock a refundable stake in escrow before trading, like a ship paying harbor dues before it may dock. A newcomer with no history starts in a shallow lagoon of low trust: tiny transaction limits and slow settlement. Good behavior over time deepens its channel, while fraud triggers slashing of the stake. Because each fake identity must post its own stake, spawning thousands costs the attacker real capital, and like yarrow spreading only where soil allows, identities grow only through sustained honest work, not mass creation.
